  WHY: The guard can miss a push inside nested shell control flow and fail open.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:lines 324-339 | severity=medium | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The `case` arm handling only searches for the end of the first arm and may not process subsequent arms.
  WHY: A `git push` in a later arm can be overlooked, allowing a push without the necessary checks.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py and workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:_evaluate_bash | severity=medium | confidence=[4]

  WHY: The operator sees the block message without the diagnostic that the command directory was uncertain.

  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_2]

  WHY: This can mark the working directory uncertain and trigger a spurious confirmation prompt.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:~lines 1474-1496 in the PR | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Confirmation reasons are combined without deduplication.
  WHY: If the same reason appears in multiple lists, the user sees it repeated in the confirmation message.

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:_command_after_control_prefix (added by LAST RUN DIFF, deployment at both _guarded_git_invocations and git_subcommands call sites) and _SHELL_CONTROL_PREFIXES | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `_command_after_control_prefix` does not handle Bash negation `!`, so both git-detection paths skip a push in `if ! git push origin; then :; fi`.
  WHY: Bash executes the push regardless of `!`, but the guard returns without checking PR state.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py and workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:_evaluate_bash, the LAST RUN DIFF removal of _warn(invocation.warning) from the push-warning block (replaced by uncertain_push_reasons.append, which is consumed only in the non-blocked confirmation path after the early return on blocks) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Uncertain-directory warnings are not emitted when a blocked push returns early.
  WHY: The operator loses the diagnostic that the guard could not resolve the command directory.
- Requirement: "Fail closed for pushes when shell control flow or the effective directory cannot be determined" (issue #6289 recommendation, third sentence)
  Expected change site: _command_after_control_prefix in .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py (added by the LAST RUN DIFF)
  Evidence of absence: The LAST RUN DIFF added _command_after_control_prefix that strips `if`, `then`, `do`, `for`, `while`, etc. but does not handle `!` negation. When `!` follows a control prefix (e.g. `if ! git push`, `while ! git push`), both git-detection paths miss the push. The tests added in the LAST RUN DIFF test `if true; then git push`, `if git push; then`, `for...do git push`, and case arms, but not `!` negation. Testing for `!` negation was the concrete gap in otherwise complete control-word coverage.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py (lines 324-339) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `_command_after_control_prefix` removes only a single shell control prefix token and does not re-evaluate the remaining tokens.
  WHY: Nested shell control flow can leave an additional prefix before `git push`, causing detection to miss the command and fail open.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py (lines 324-339) and git_subcommands (lines 714) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Shell negation (`!`) causes the guard to parse the command incorrectly.
  WHY: The git detection expects `git` first after stripping assignments and control words; with `!` present it can miss the push and fail open.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py (lines 329-335) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `case`-arm logic only searches for the end of the first arm and does not process subsequent case arms.
  WHY: A `git push` in a later arm can be overlooked without the necessary checks.
- Requirement: "Fail closed for pushes when shell control flow or the effective directory cannot be determined" (issue #6289 recommendation, third sentence).
  Expected change site: `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py`, `_command_after_control_prefix`
  Evidence of absence: The current implementation of `_command_after_control_prefix` is insufficient to satisfy this requirement because it does not handle nested control flow (it only peels one layer) or shell negation (`!`), nor does it robustly handle all `case` arm permutations. As a result, the guard does not truly "fail closed" in these cases.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

  PROBLEM: The parser strips `if` but does not handle a following shell negation operator (`!`), so `git_subcommands()` does not recognize the push in `if ! git push origin; then :; fi`.
  WHY: Bash executes `git push`; `_evaluate_bash()` sees no guarded subcommand and returns without checking merged-PR status or requesting confirmation.
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:`_command_after_control_prefix()` (lines 327-339 in diff) as called by `git_subcommands()` (~line 717) and `_guarded_git_invocations()` (~line 384) | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Shell negation `!` after a control word bypasses both git-detection paths.

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:_command_after_control_prefix (lines ~327-339 in the PR), called from _guarded_git_invocations (~line 384) and git_subcommands (~line 717) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `_command_after_control_prefix` does not handle the Bash negation reserved word `!`.
  WHY: A command such as `if ! git push origin; then echo fail; fi` executes the push but bypasses the guard, with no merged-PR check or confirmation.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:_command_after_control_prefix, the `if tokens and tokens[0].endswith(")")` branch (~line 337 in the PR) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The unconditional `endswith(")")` check can strip tokens that are not case-arm patterns and set `control_prefix` to true.
  WHY: This can cause a false-positive confirmation prompt for a command whose working directory is not uncertain.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:_evaluate_bash confirmation logic (~lines 1474-1496 in the PR) | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: Confirmation reasons are combined without deduplication.
  WHY: Duplicate reason text can appear in the confirmation message.
- Requirement: "Fail closed for pushes when shell control flow or the effective directory cannot be determined" (issue #6289 recommendation, third sentence).
  Expected change site: _command_after_control_prefix in .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py and the matching workflow-templates copy.
  Evidence of absence: _command_after_control_prefix handles if/then/elif/else/do/while/until/{/(/case but not the bash `!` negation reserved word. After stripping a control word, if the next token is `!`, the git command behind it is not detected and the push is allowed without any check. No test covers `if ! git push origin; then :; fi`. The LAST RUN DIFF added control-word handling but left `!` unhandled, so the "fail closed" recommendation is only partially implemented for shell control flow.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
